page.overview:
What is Kanto?

Kanto is a region introduced in Generation I.

Kanto is the original region introduced in the Pokémon franchise. It was then followed by Johto, Hoenn, Sinnoh, Unova, Kalos, Alola, Galar, and Paldea. It is modeled and named after the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kant%C5%8D_region Kantō region of Japan], which includes, amongst other cities, the capital Tōkyō, where Game Freak is headquartered. Kanto is the only one that shares its name with a real-world location. The resemblance between the bay formations seen on the in-game map and the actual Sagami Bay, Suruga Bay, and Tokyo Bay formations is particularly striking. Kanto also has some elements of Chūbu.

Kanto lies to the east of Johto; they presumably make up a small continent; to the south of Kanto are the Sevii and Orange Islands. Hoenn, introduced in and , is supposedly further to the southwest. Routes located wholly within Kanto are numbered 1 to 25; routes 26, 27, and 28 connect Kanto with Johto. Supposedly to the north of this continent is the Sinnoh region. Unova is in a considerable distance away and it's unknown where both it and Kalos are in relation to Kanto.

In the first generation of games for the Game Boy, and , Kanto was the only region to explore, featuring a variety of environments, such as urban locales and mountainous, wooded and oceanic routes. In Gold, Silver and Crystal, which introduced Johto as a neighboring region to its west, the player character was able to travel to Kanto (by either steamboat, surfing or the magnet train) travelling between Goldenrod City in Johto and Saffron City in Kanto after completing their journeys through the latter. Since the Generation II games occupied an in-universe timeline a few years after their predecessors, some changes were introduced. In late 2004, Pocket Monsters Red Version and Pocket Monsters Green Version were remade as new titles for the Game Boy Advance called Pokémon FireRed and LeafGreen, which incorporated new elements. In late 2018, Pokémon Yellow was remade as two new games for the Nintendo Switch, .
